text:
support_julia: FYI customer ACME reporting 503/429 errors to Dedicated in us-west2 starting ~02:15 UTC. Ticket INC-2026-458 created. They see high tail latency and placement failures.

sre-oncall: :rotating_light: grabbing it. Any correlation with autoscaler events or reserve-pool changes?

emily: I see placement rejections in the allocator logs: 
```
2026-03-17T02:14:52Z WARN placement failed: reason=insufficient_gpus required=4 available=0 pool=reserved-usw2
```
Looks like reserve pool hit zero.

ryan: Confirmed. Autoscale didn't bring up new nodes — scale-up request backlog shows repeated throttles: 
```
scale_request id=aa12 status=rate_limited reason=region_quota
```
That was between 02:10-02:18.

aman: Could be cross-tenant oversubscription in that AZ. Metrics show a noisy-tenant eviction spike at 02:08 (tenant id redacted). VM churn + preemption on spot-backed machines.

sre-oncall: Is this strictly capacity (stockout) or a placement bug? We should rule out auth/billing.

billing-bot: ACME account billing/quotas normal. No overdue or quota block. (checked at 02:20 UTC).

support_julia: Customer mentioned no change from their side. They also attempted to retry and saw immediate 429s. Provided request example and timestamp.

emily: I pulled edge logs for their route: consistent 503 on route /v1/generate -> inference-runtime returned 503 with error "placement_failed". No auth failures.

ryan: Repro steps for us: 
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.test/dedicated/us-west2/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -d '{"model":"gpt-neo-16k","batch_size":8,"prompt":"test"}'
2) Observe 503 placement_failed in response.

ops-bot: Created internal incident INC-2026-458-ops and attached allocation logs.

sre-oncall: Quick mitigation proposal: 1) enable cross-region failover for ACME to na-central (they're on enterprise and allowed fallback) 2) temporarily increase reserved pool for us-west2 from 0 -> 4 using manual allocation 3) enable burst-capacity for high-priority customers. Thoughts?

aman: Steps to confirm noisy neighbor: check per-tenant gpu_util and eviction counts on nodes provisioning at 02:00-02:12. I have traces showing tenant X did sustained 95-99% GPU util for the period and caused scheduler preemptions.

emily: I can push a hotfix to allocator to surface clearer error codes (insufficient_gpus -> noisy_neighbor_preemption) but that's low-risk and helps debugging.

ryan: For immediate relief I've queued a manual reservation: `admin reserve --region us-west2 --pool reserved-usw2 --gpus 4 --ttl 6h` — provisioning underway (02:25 UTC).

support_julia: Customer asked for ETA. What do we tell them?

sre-oncall: Tell them ~15-25m for manual reserve show-up + validation, offer to reroute to na-central (5-10m) if acceptable. Also add apology + postmortem promise.

billing-bot: Noting that enabling burst-capacity will incur on-demand charges; notify account team before enabling for >1h.

aman: Postmortem checklist: capture allocator logs, autoscaler logs, node provisioning traces, per-tenant GPU metrics, and customer request traces. Mark any quota hits in cloud provider console.

emily: Quick repro/test for the team to validate fix: 
```
# simulate heavy tenant on a test pool
python tools/sim_noisy_tenant.py --region us-west2 --gpus 8 --duration 600
# then try placement for small reserved request
curl -X POST https://internal.infra/dryrun/placement -d '{"gpus":4,"model":"gpt-neo-16k"}'
```

ryan: After manual reserve applied, early signs look good — one ACME request succeeded at 02:32 UTC. Need to watch for additional reclamation.

sre-oncall: Keep monitoring for next 30m. If we see repeat, escalate to platform infra for quota request with cloud provider or recommend customer failover permanently.

support_julia: Customer updated: they accepted failover to na-central for the short term and are happy with reroute. Asking for root cause and timeline for permanent fix.

ops-bot: Added action items: (1) manual reserve applied, (2) enable failover for ACME, (3) collect logs and run noisy-tenant simulation, (4) follow-up postmortem. Owner tags: ryan/emily/aman.

emily: Note — autoscaler rate-limited by region_quota is concerning; we should add alert to ops when scale_request rate_limited > 5 within 10m. Filing infra ticket INFRA-2026-77.

aman: TL;DR: root cause appears to be regional GPU scarcity amplified by a noisy tenant causing preemptions + autoscaler rate limits preventing automatic refill. Mitigations applied: manual reserve + customer failover. Postmortem and follow-ups assigned.

support_julia: I'll close the customer loop and update INC-2026-458 with the actions and ETA for postmortem. Thanks everyone :heart: 

sre-oncall: Closing here after 30m warm-up if metrics stable. Will reopen if errors reappear.

emily: saving logs -> s3://redwood-ops/incidents/INC-2026-458/logs (redacted link).

ryan: final note: please add billing contact before leaving burst-capacity enabled.

ops-bot: Incident marked triaged.
